reason:
Every number in the finding reproduces, on both grounds, and the refutations I tried all fail on measurement. REPRODUCED. Driven at 390x844, 768x1024, 1280x900 and 1440x960, v=paper and v=ink, state=owner-flight, scrolled to the foot of the measure, press Preview, press Back to the plan: scrollY 1184->0 at 390, 1483->0 at 768, 107->0 at 1280 and 1440; activeElement is H1.b-who in all eight runs; 0 page errors. Before the round trip the last row on screen is Wedding day and the first is Choose the evening music; after it the first row on screen is Menu tasting at The Orchard, the first row of the plan, at every width and on both grounds. I also drove the real loop the finding names (open the last row, press the stepper, Done, Preview, Back, at 390 and 1440): same result - scrollY 1171 / pane 1021 before, 0 / 0 after, the editor closed, the row nowhere near the viewport.

THE DESK CASE IS BIGGER THAN THE FINDING REPORTS, NOT SMALLER. The finding cites 107->0 at 1279 and 1280, and 107 is the lab furniture SETTLED already ruled on (desk-frame-still-scrolls: 40px stage-pad + 15px caption + 12px gap + 40px). But at desk widths the owner's scroll actually happens in the .b-plan pane, and paneOf() returns it: measured pane.scrollTop 1103->0 at 1280x900 and 1043->0 at 1440x960, on both grounds. So the transition discards between 1043 and 1483 pixels of place at every width tested. The finding under-measured its own strongest case; that is not a reason to kill it.

IS THE RETURN TO THE TOP ARGUABLY CORRECT - the head carries the count and the day? No, and at desk it is void. Measured: at 1280 and 1440 .b-ownerField .b-stick computes position:sticky and .b-todayLabel sits at y=408 IN VIEW at pane.scrollTop = max, i.e. the count and the day never left the screen, so returning to the top buys the owner nothing they did not already have - it only spends 1043-1103px. (SETTLED pinned-label-stops-naming-what-is-under-it and today-stated-twice-in-two-grammars both rest on that same sticky horizon.) At 390 and 768 the horizon does scroll away (position:static, labelTop -778 / -937 at the foot), so the top does re-show the day - to an owner who set it and has been reading it all session, at the price of a whole measure.

IS IT THE SETTLED preview-erases-the-way-back UNDER A NEW NAME? No. That one is the undo STACK being cleared by history.length = 0 inside render(state), and it died on two grounds neither of which reaches here. (a) Harness scope: history.length = 0 fires on every remount including the console chooser and the ground flip, so restoring it would leak across lab state jumps. A place restore hung on the module-level flag fires only when the owner presses [data-act=owner]; console.shell.html goes through api.setState + api.mount and never through that click handler, so it cannot leak into a chooser jump or a direct load. (b) Nothing visible: that verdict refused the fix because "not one pixel, one string or one gesture changes", and the only visible variant of it made the screen worse. Here the fix is nothing BUT what is on screen - which row the owner is standing in front of when the plan comes back.

IS PREVIEW A FULL STATE CHANGE WHERE LOSING SCROLL IS HONEST? Going TO the preview, yes, and the finding concedes it. Coming back is not a surface the owner is arriving at, it is one they were standing in ninety seconds ago, and this product has already decided that question against itself three times in code: remember() writes entry.at = window.scrollY and entry.paneAt = pane.scrollTop under the comment "The place the owner was looking at is part of the change. Undo used to restore the moment and leave them a screen away from it", and undo() replays both in a finally block; holdingPlace() holds pane.scrollTop across a mutation because "a scroller re-anchors on its own terms"; keepInBand() scrolls the edited row into the free band. The precedent is not merely applicable - it is the same author, the same paneOf accessor and the same two numbers.

THE GATE DOES NOT COVER IT, and this is not a restatement. interaction-check.mjs:1414-1421 asserts only that .b-item count survives the round trip; :1487 asserts activeElement !== body and a non-empty live region. Every scroll assertion in the gate is elsewhere - :473/:493 ("the page keeps its place through the move", the stepper), :2106, :2591, :3454, :3614 - and none reads an offset across Preview/Back. The gate already asserts this exact principle by name for the stepper and never once for this transition.

TWO CODE ERRORS IN THE PROPOSED FIX, corrected in sharpenedFix, neither fatal: go() ALREADY passes preventScroll (render-b.js:1542), and there is no requestAnimationFrame in go() - the head focus is synchronous, so the restore has to sit after C.mount() in the return branch. I drove the fix's mechanics by replaying the captured place two frames after the remount at all four widths: scrollY returns to 1184 / 1483 / 107 / 107 and pane.scrollTop to 0 / 0 / 1103 / 1043 exactly, the first visible row is the one the owner left (Choose the evening music at phone and tablet, Final guest numbers at desk), and the restore sticks - the existing preventScroll means nothing undoes it. 0 page errors.

One residual the finding does not see, and the sharpened fix must handle it: restoring place while leaving focus on .b-who puts the focused element a measure off screen, so a keyboard owner's next Tab yanks the page straight back to the top - reinstating the defect for the reader who can least afford it.
sharpenedFix:
Scope it to the owner's own return leg, and make focus and viewport agree.

(1) In wireOwner's click handler on [data-act=preview] (render-b.js:1366), before go("desk"), capture onto a module-level var beside cameFromOwner (which already survives the remount): var pane0 = paneOf(root); var mark = root.querySelector('.b-item[data-editing="true"]') || topmostItemIn(root); cameBack = { y: window.scrollY, pane: pane0 ? pane0.scrollTop : null, id: mark && mark.getAttribute("data-id") }. Capture the row id, not only the offsets: the plan can be shorter on return (a hide, a delete), and a raw offset then clamps onto the wrong row. Do the same on [data-act=publish] (:1367) so the publish round trip returns the same way.

(2) In the three [data-act=owner] branches (render-b.js:1368, :1636, :1964), after go("owner-flight") - go() is synchronous and its head.focus already passes preventScroll at :1542, so do not add a second preventScroll and do not look for an rAF that does not exist - run one requestAnimationFrame, re-query the fresh root (var back = document.querySelector(".b-field"); var pane = paneOf(back)), then: if the remembered id is still present, put that row back in the same band keepInBand uses - in the pane when paneOf returns one, in the window when it does not; otherwise fall back to window.scrollTo(0, cameBack.y) and pane.scrollTop = cameBack.pane.

(3) Then move focus to that row's .b-grab with preventScroll instead of leaving it on .b-who, so the keyboard owner's focus sits inside the restored view and the next Tab does not throw the page back to the top. The live region already carries "Back to the plan.", so the announcement does not depend on the heading holding focus. Fall back to the head only when no row survived.

(4) Clear cameBack once replayed, so a later direct load or a console chooser jump into owner-flight stays byte-identical to today.

(5) Gate, written first and failing: at 390, 768, 1280 and 1440, on paper and on ink, scroll owner-flight to its foot (the window at phone and tablet, the .b-plan pane at desk), record the topmost .b-item data-id and the offset, press Preview, press Back, and assert BOTH that the same data-id is on screen and Math.abs(offset - before) <= 2 in whichever scroller paneOf names. The desk half must read pane.scrollTop: the window's 107 there is lab furniture, and an assertion written against it would prove nothing - the class of passing-but-empty assertion this round was told to hunt.
